name: Mexico City
tagline: The mole that's been fermenting for over a decade, and the street taco that won — then lost — a Michelin star.

Pujol.description: Avant-garde Mexican cuisine from Jorge Vallejo and Alejandra Flores. The mole madre, fermenting for over a decade now, is the house signature.

El Califa de León.description: The world's first taquería to hold a Michelin star (2024) — and also the first to lose it (2026). The gaonera taco that broke the internet.

Siembra Comedor.description: A tortillería and dining room devoted to heirloom corn in Polanco. It's the only tortillería recognized by the Michelin Guide, with a Bib Gourmand.

El Cardenal.description: Breakfasts of conchas with cream and hot chocolate since 1969, in the heart of the Historic Center.

El Huequito.description: A Centro Histórico taquería known for its tacos al pastor. Anthony Bourdain tried them on 'No Reservations' and called them "shockingly good."

Quintonil.description: Seasonal cooking from Jorge Vallejo and Alejandra Flores in Polanco, with its own kitchen garden. Two Michelin stars and No. 3 on The World's 50 Best Restaurants list in 2025.

Sud 777.description: Edgar Núñez's restaurant in Jardines del Pedregal, built around ingredients from local growers and its own garden. Holds one Michelin star.

Rosetta.description: Elena Reygadas's restaurant in a Porfirian-era mansion in Roma Norte, crossing Italian technique with Mexican seasonal ingredients. Holds one Michelin star.

Em.description: Chef Lucho Martínez's project built around seasonal Mexican cooking and house-made ferments. Holds one Michelin star since 2024.

Esquina Común.description: A dining room built around corn and preservation and fermentation techniques. Holds one Michelin star.

Expendio de Maíz.description: No fixed menu — the kitchen decides what to serve each night based on the corn and seasonal ingredients on hand. Holds one Michelin star.

Masala y Maíz.description: Chefs Norma Listman and Saqib Keval fuse their roots in India, East Africa and Mexico. Holds one Michelin star.

Máximo Bistrot.description: Chef Eduardo García's market-driven bistro in Roma Norte, blending French technique with Mexican ingredients. Anthony Bourdain dined here on 'Parts Unknown' (2014); it now holds a Michelin star.

La Once Mil.description: A seasonal Mexican restaurant in Miguel Hidalgo, awarded a Michelin star.

Contramar.description: Roma Norte's most popular seafood dining room since 1998, from chef Gabriela Cámara. The pescado a la talla and tuna tostada are reason enough to line up without a reservation. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Taquería Los Cocuyos.description: A 24-hour sidewalk taquería in the Centro Histórico, famous for its eye-meat and suadero tacos. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

El Vilsito.description: By day it's an auto-parts shop; by night the al pastor spit rolls out to the sidewalk and it becomes one of the city's most beloved taquerías. Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Taquería El Jarocho.description: A Cuauhtémoc taquería awarded a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide for the quality of its stewed-meat and carnitas tacos.

Tacos Charly.description: A neighborhood taquería in Tlalpan distinguished with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Taquería Los Milanesos.description: Milanesa-taco specialists in Álvaro Obregón, awarded a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Raíz.description: A Mexican dining room in Miguel Hidalgo recognized with a Bib Gourmand for its value for money.

Comedor Jacinta.description: A home-style Mexican dining room in Polanco, recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Comal Oculto.description: Comal-driven Mexican cooking in Miguel Hidalgo, distinguished with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Los Consentidos del Barrio.description: A Benito Juárez taquería recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Galanga Thai House.description: Thai cooking in Cuauhtémoc, uncommon for the city, recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Vigneron.description: A French-inspired bistro in Cuauhtémoc with an extensive wine list, recognized with a Bib Gourmand.

Pargot.description: Mexican seafood cooking in Cuauhtémoc, recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Filigrana.description: Chef-driven Mexican cooking in Cuauhtémoc, recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Fugaz.description: Cooking that crosses the Mediterranean with Mexico in Roma, recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Caracol de Mar.description: A seafood bar with Peruvian influences in Roma, recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Jowong.description: Korean cooking in Cuauhtémoc, recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Galea.description: An Italian trattoria in Roma, recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Ultramarinos Demar.description: A Spanish-style seafood and tinned-fish bar in Cuauhtémoc, recognized with a Bib Gourmand by the Michelin Guide.

Handshake Speakeasy.description: A speakeasy hidden inside a hotel in Colonia Juárez, named Best Bar in North America at North America's 50 Best Bars two years running.

Licorería Limantour.description: The cocktail bar that put Roma Norte on the world map; a regular on The World's 50 Best Bars list for over a decade.

Baltra Bar.description: A neighborhood bar with a café-like setting and finely honed classic cocktails, from the team behind Licorería Limantour. A regular on North America's 50 Best Bars.

Cantina La Mascota.description: A classic cantina downtown where Anthony Bourdain ate carnitas and a fava-bean-and-cactus soup during his Mexico City visit on 'No Reservations'.

Nicos.description: A family institution in Clavería, run by Gerardo Vázquez Lugo, a benchmark for traditional Mexican cooking and an early champion of cooking with local growers' ingredients.

Dulce Patria.description: Chef Martha Ortiz's restaurant in Polanco, Mexican cooking staged as theater — color, national symbols and historically inspired dishes.

Merotoro.description: Chef Jair Téllez's restaurant, bringing Baja California's seafood-and-vineyard cooking to Condesa.

Sartoria.description: Hand-made pasta cooking in Roma Norte, one of the city's best-regarded Italian restaurants.

Ticuchi.description: Enrique Olvera's project in Pujol's original Polanco space: pescatarian Oaxacan cooking alongside an extensive mezcal and agave-spirits list.

Casa Virginia.description: Chef Mónica Patiño's culinary legacy in Roma, Mexican-rooted cooking with French influence in a family-house setting.

Tetetlán.description: A café and restaurant inside a house designed by Luis Barragán in Jardines del Pedregal, serving Mesoamerican-rooted cooking alongside a local design shop.

Molino El Pujol.description: Enrique Olvera's mill and bakery next to Pujol in Polanco, specializing in sourdough bread made with nixtamalized corn.

Lardo.description: A Mediterranean-leaning restaurant-bakery in Condesa, popular for breakfast and its house-baked bread.

Panadería Rosetta.description: Rosetta's sister bakery in Roma Norte, famous for its guava-filled concha, which regularly sells out before noon.

Café Nin.description: Elena Reygadas's café in Roma Norte with its own bakery, built for breakfasts and light lunches.

Huset.description: A Scandinavian-inspired restaurant in Roma Norte, applying Nordic fermentation techniques to Mexican ingredients.

Meroma.description: Merotoro's sister restaurant in Roma Norte, open-fire cooking with Mexican and Mediterranean influences.

Anatol.description: A neighborhood restaurant in Condesa serving contemporary Mexican cooking on a short, frequently changing menu.

El Parnita.description: A contemporary antojería in Roma Norte, always packed, famous for its tuna tostada and shrimp tacos.

Rokai.description: An izakaya in Escandón, part of chef Daniel Ovadía's group of Japanese restaurants, known for its grilled yakitori.

Le Tachinomi Desu.description: A Japanese standing bar next to Rokai in Escandón, modeled on Japan's tachinomiya, for sake and quick bites.

Tori Tori.description: A benchmark Japanese restaurant in Polanco, one of the pioneers of high-end Japanese cooking in the city.

Kaito Del Valle.description: An omakase sushi counter in Colonia Del Valle, specializing in fish imported directly from Japan.

Café Tacuba.description: A Centro Histórico restaurant open since 1912, with original tilework, stone-ground chocolate and a house mariachi band; the rock band Café Tacvba took its name from here.

El Moro.description: A churrería in the Centro open since 1935, serving churros and hot chocolate around the clock.

San Ángel Inn.description: A restaurant set inside a 17th-century former Carmelite convent in San Ángel, celebrated for its margaritas and classic Mexican cooking.

Hostería de Santo Domingo.description: The city's oldest restaurant, open since 1860 near Plaza Santo Domingo; its signature dish is chiles en nogada.

La Opera Bar.description: A Centro Histórico cantina open since 1876, famous for the bullet hole in its ceiling that legend attributes to Pancho Villa during the Revolution.

Salón Tenampa.description: A cantina founded in 1925 on Plaza Garibaldi, the cradle of the city's mariachi tradition; it turned one hundred years old in 2025.

Salón Corona.description: A chain of Centro Histórico cantinas founded in 1928, a classic stop for draft beer and antojitos.

Fonda Margarita.description: A Del Valle breakfast fonda that opens at dawn, no written menu, famous for its lard-cooked beans.

Dulcería de Celaya.description: A Centro Histórico sweet shop open since 1874, wooden cases full of traditional Mexican candies like milk jamoncillo and candied sweet potato.

Pastelería Ideal.description: A giant Centro bakery open since 1927, several floors of sweet bread and celebration cakes.

Los Bisquets Obregón.description: A café chain founded in 1958, a classic for café de olla, sweet bread and full Mexican breakfasts.

Sanborns Casa de los Azulejos.description: A restaurant set inside the 18th-century Palacio de los Azulejos, the flagship Sanborns location since 1919, famous for its patio and Tiffany stained-glass ceiling.

Coox Hanal.description: A third-floor Yucatecan dining room in the Centro Histórico since 1953, cochinita pibil, panuchos and lime soup, with a live trío on weekends.

El Rey del Pavo.description: A Centro Histórico torta shop founded in 1910, the oldest in the city, specializing in turkey tortas.

Taquería Orinoco.description: A taquería chain born in Condesa, popular for its pineapple-topped al pastor tacos and neighborhood vibe.

Antojitos La Guadalupana.description: A neighborhood cantina in Coyoacán, always packed, famous for its squash-blossom quesadillas and grilled beef.

Los Danzantes.description: A pioneer of mezcal-driven Mexican cooking in Coyoacán, open since 1994 facing the Jardín Centenario.

Corazón de Maguey.description: A mezcal bar with a terrace facing Coyoacán's Jardín Centenario, one of the city's most complete mezcal lists.

El Bajío.description: A restaurant founded by Carmen 'Titita' Ramírez Degollado, a benchmark for regional Mexican cooking and basket tacos since its original Azcapotzalco location.

Fonda San Ángel.description: A restaurant facing Plaza San Jacinto in San Ángel, traditional Mexican cooking in a colonial setting, popular on Saturday Bazaar days.

La Casa de Toño.description: A chain that started in Roma, famous for its pozole and its endless lines; one of the city's most beloved and most photographed fondas on social media.

Mercado de San Juan.description: A gourmet market in the Centro specializing in exotic and seasonal ingredients, from imported cheeses to edible insects; a supply stop for many of the city's chefs.

Mercado Roma.description: A two-story food hall in Roma Norte, with dozens of food stalls and a craft-beer rooftop terrace.

Mercado de Coyoacán.description: A traditional market in Coyoacán, famous for its tostada stalls and antojitos served amid flower and craft stands.

Mercado de Medellín.description: A market in Colonia Roma with a strong Latin American immigrant presence, known for its Cuban, Venezuelan and Caribbean food stalls.

La Merced.description: The city's largest and oldest traditional market, the historic hub for fruit, vegetables and street food supply.

El Tizoncito.description: A Condesa taquería opened in 1966 by Concepción 'Doña Conchita' Cervantes, credited with inventing the taco al pastor.

El Farolito.description: A very popular al pastor taquería in Condesa, open into the small hours.

El Fogoncito.description: An al pastor taquería chain with several branches around the city, a classic late-night stop.

El Turix.description: A street stand in Polanco specializing solely in cochinita pibil, as a taco, torta, panucho or tamal; founded by Arturo Nabté, of Maya origin.

El Pescadito.description: A Baja California-style fish-and-shrimp taco chain, with branches across the city.

Fisher's.description: A classic seafood chain in the city since the 1970s, old-school shrimp cocktail and breaded fish.

Café El Jarocho.description: A Coyoacán coffee stand since 1953, café de olla and cappuccino served in a paper cup to go, always with a line out the door.

Cafebrería El Péndulo.description: A bookstore chain with an in-house café, with branches in Roma and Condesa set among plants and bookshelves.

Buna.description: A specialty-coffee roaster and café with several branches across Roma and Condesa, part of the city's third-wave coffee scene.

Almanegra Café.description: A specialty coffee shop born in 2014, minimalist and detail-obsessed, a benchmark of the Roma Norte coffee scene.

Maque.description: A Roma bakery known for its sourdough bread and French pastry, very popular for weekend breakfasts.

La Docena.description: An oyster and seafood bar in Roma Norte, a modern-cantina vibe with chef-driven cocktails.

Broka Bistrot.description: A bistro tucked into the patio of a Roma Norte mansion, French cooking with Mexican accents.

Cicatriz Café.description: A Condesa café with several branches around the city, popular for working and for international-style breakfasts.

Blanco Colima.description: A restaurant in a Porfirian-era building in Roma Norte since 2015, with one of the city's most extensive mezcal lists.

Bósforo.description: An unpretentious mezcal bar in the Centro Histórico, rustic atmosphere and one of the city's best mezcal selections.

Cantina Tío Pepe.description: The city's oldest cantina, open since 1869 on Motolinía street; it keeps its original interior, including the table bells once used to call the waiter.

La Casa de las Sirenas.description: A restaurant inside a 16th-century building steps from the Zócalo, with a 1754 terrace overlooking the Templo Mayor; traditional Mexican cooking and over 200 mezcals.
